chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, raising it, from Abān, said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A young woman among us has an ulcer within her, and blood is flowing; she does not know whether it is from menstrual blood or from the blood of the ulcer.

He said: "Tell her to lie on her back, raise her legs, and insert her middle finger. Then if the blood comes out from the left side, it is from menstruation; and if it comes out from the right side, then it is from the ulcer."

key_terms.الدَّمُ: the blood under examination for legal determination
key_terms.الْجَانِبِ الْأَيْسَرِ: the left side, identified here as indicating menstrual blood
key_terms.الْجَانِبِ الْأَيْمَنِ: the right side, identified here as indicating ulcer blood
key_terms.دَمِ الْحَيْضِ: menstrual blood, which carries specific legal rulings
key_terms.دَمِ الْقَرْحَةِ: blood originating from the ulcer rather than menstruation
key_terms.قَرْحَةٌ: an ulcer or wound causing internal bleeding

ai.seo_question: How can menstrual blood be distinguished from ulcer blood in Shia fiqh when a woman is uncertain?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal criterion for distinguishing menstrual blood from blood caused by an internal ulcer when uncertainty exists. It reflects the Imamic fiqh concern with determining ritual status accurately in cases affecting rulings of taharah and acts of worship.
